notes: Repaired during the goal-desk-iter-15 audit: the authored script embedded three JavaScript regex literals (/history.*sessions/, /BRK-B/, /2026-07-29/) inside JSON, so demo_runner.py could not parse it at all and the whole lane recorded SKIPPED with zero screenshots. Every target is now a plain JSON string, and every step's action now matches what its own narration claims (three steps previously narrated a hover or a fallback while their action navigated somewhere else).
Deliberately read-only: no step clicks Run Screen or any compute trigger, so re-recording this walkthrough never writes a new snapshot and never touches the append-only screen rail.

Capture geometry: demo_runner.py records a 1280x800 viewport (not a full-page shot), and the short-history name in the current ambient store (HONA, 27 sessions) ranks #8 -- just below that fold at the top of the page. Steps 8 and 9 therefore walk down to the Screen History ledger and back up to the ranked table's history header, which leaves the briefing scrolled so a >= 400-session row and the <= 60-session row are legible in the SAME frame. The DoD's own one-screenshot short/long proof is independently held by the browser-QA evidence (reports/qa/goal-desk-iter-15-evidence/UT-02-result.png and TC-08-history-column.png, both 1400x2200).

The composite row tooltip is a native HTML title attribute; a browser never paints it into a screenshot. Step 4 therefore narrates it and points at the anchor that carries it -- browser-QA read the attribute directly (UT-03: 'distance 0 bps - score 51 - basis 2026-07-23T04:00:00.000000Z (5 d before as-of) - history 27 sessions from 2026-06-15T04:00:00.000000Z - ...').

steps.title: Open the Desk briefing
steps.narration: The Desk page shows the latest recorded screen over the registered universe: a ranked table of tradable walls, read verbatim from the persisted snapshot. Nothing on this page is recomputed in the browser.
steps.point_out: The heading reads 'Desk', and the Provenance panel pins the exact screen this page is showing: universe snapshot, screen date, as-of, config fingerprint, and bar-store signature.

steps.title: The briefing table gains a history column
steps.narration: This iteration adds one column to the ranked table: history. It sits immediately right of the existing basis column and says how much completed daily history each row's wall was measured over.
steps.point_out: The header row now reads symbol, side, class, distance, score, coverage, tick evidence, basis, and — new — history.

steps.title: Every ranked row states its own history depth
steps.narration: Each row now carries its own count of completed daily sessions at or before that row's basis bar, plus the date that history starts from. In the store this walkthrough runs against the counts span 27 to 501 across the same screen, so a recently listed name no longer looks identical to one with two years of sessions.
steps.point_out: Read the history cell on any row: 'history 500 sessions - from 2024-07-25'. It is a plain count and a date — no score, no threshold, no judgement about whether that is enough.

steps.title: Full precision lives in the row's existing tooltip
steps.narration: The cell shows the start date rounded to a day. The untruncated timestamp is not lost: it joins the row drill-in anchor's one composite hover tooltip, beside the distance, score and basis details that were already there. No second tooltip mechanism was added.
steps.point_out: Hovering a row's symbol shows one tooltip ending with 'history 27 sessions from 2026-06-15T04:00:00.000000Z'. A native title tooltip is not painted into a screenshot — browser-QA read the attribute directly (UT-03).

steps.title: Open a screen recorded before this feature shipped
steps.narration: Screen snapshots are append-only: an already-recorded screen is never rewritten or backfilled. Clicking an older row in Screen History swaps that exact persisted snapshot into the page.
steps.point_out: The banner confirms which snapshot is on screen: 'Viewing the recorded screen for 2026-07-29 — not the latest.'

steps.title: A legacy row says so, instead of inventing a number
steps.narration: That snapshot was recorded before this iteration's code existed, so its rows carry no history fields at all. The page says exactly that rather than showing a zero, a blank, or the word null.
steps.point_out: Every history cell now reads 'history not recorded in this snapshot', while the basis column beside it still shows its own real per-row values.

expect.text: history not recorded in this snapshot

steps.title: Return to the latest screen
steps.narration: The Latest button in Screen History drops the pinned older snapshot and puts the most recently recorded screen back on the page.
steps.point_out: The 'not the latest' banner disappears once the latest screen is displayed again.

steps.title: The append-only screen ledger below the briefing
steps.narration: Below the ranked table, Screen History lists every screen ever recorded, each with its own row/skip counts and its own provenance pins. Nothing here was rewritten by this iteration — the older snapshots are exactly the bytes they were recorded as.
steps.point_out: One row per recorded screen: date, rows, skipped, and the universe snapshot, config fingerprint and bar-store signature that screen was pinned to.

steps.title: A 27-session listing beside a 500-session name
steps.narration: Back up at the briefing, the whole point of the column is legible in one frame: rows at the top carry 500 completed sessions dating from July 2024, while HONA — ranked eighth on the same scale — carries 27, from June 2026. Before this iteration those two rows were indistinguishable.
steps.point_out: Compare BRK-B's 'history 500 sessions - from 2024-07-25' with HONA's 'history 27 sessions - from 2026-06-15', both visible in this single view.
